profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap record sits within an industrial landuse area in Davidson County, Tennessee, part of Nashville, and is tagged as a telecom data center under the name Tennessee Processing Center LLC at an address on Woodfolk Avenue. The surrounding area, near Brick Church Park, does host real back office and financial processing operations for larger companies, and the name Tennessee Processing Center is consistent with a document, forms, or transaction processing business of the kind that can run substantial internal server infrastructure to support day to day operations.

Business directory listings for this specific address, however, categorize Tennessee Processing Center under household and business organizing services, list it as roughly two decades old, and show standard weekday office hours rather than the round the clock staffing typical of a colocation data center. No operator website, technical specifications, or public description of server, power, or cooling infrastructure at this address could be located. That combination, a small, long running local business with limited public information and weekday only hours, is more consistent with an office based records or organizing service than with a data center built to host equipment for outside customers.

This entry is published without data center specifications because the available public record cannot confirm that this address houses the kind of dedicated IT infrastructure the telecom data center tag implies.
profile.research_note: Tennessee Processing Center LLC, 420 Woodfolk Ave, Nashville TN (Davidson County), industrial landuse polygon. Yellow Pages lists this exact business (420 Woodfolk Ave, phone 615-564-7800) under category 'Organizing Services-Household & Business', 22 years in business, Mon-Fri 8am-4pm hours, no indication of 24/7 colocation operations. Nearby Brick Church Park area does host real financial back-office/data-processing tenants (Fiserv at 575 Brick Church Park Dr, John Hancock, Comerica per MapQuest) but nothing ties this specific address/business to that kind of operation. No operator website or technical specs found. Likely mistag or at minimum an unconfirmed small local business, not a genuine colocation data center. Published as unconfirmed.

reading.body:
Tennessee Processing Center LLC adds zero confirmed megawatts to Tennessee's data center capacity; the public record describes a weekday-only organizing service, not a colocation facility, so it cannot be counted in AI infrastructure planning.

The gap between the OpenStreetMap telecom data center tag and the business record matters because AI capacity is measured in megawatts and confirmed buildings. This address has no published power figure, no operator, and no technical specifications, so it cannot support any estimate of compute or grid load.

Nearby Brick Church Park properties do house legitimate financial back-office and data processing operations, but nothing ties this specific address to them. Tennessee's confirmed capacity remains four facilities with published megawatt figures totaling 12.13 MW across 24 mapped locations, and this record does not change that total. The absence of specifications is not evidence of hidden infrastructure; it is evidence that the data center classification cannot be verified.
